text: EX-99.1 2 bccexhibit9919302026.htm EARNINGS RELEASE Document Boise Cascade Company Exhibit 99.1 1111 West Jefferson Street, Suite 300 Boise, ID 83702 Press Release For Immediate Release: November 2, 2026 Investor Contact Chris Forrey investor@bc.com Media Contact Amy Evans mediarelations@bc.com Boise Cascade reports third quarter 2026 results BOISE, IDAHO - November 2, 2026 - Boise Cascade Company ("Boise Cascade," the "Company," "we," or "our") (NYSE: BCC) today reported net income of $36.4 million, or $1.04 per share, on sales of $1.8 billion for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared with net income of $21.8 million, or $0.58 per share, on sales of $1.7 billion for the third quarter ended September 30, 2025. “In the third quarter of 2026, we delivered strong financial results despite softer housing starts, demonstrating the resilience of our integrated distribution and wood products platform,” said Jeff Strom, CEO. “Our nationwide reach, local expertise, and disciplined execution enabled us to begin navigating our supplier transitions while sustaining the reliable service and consistent value our customers count on. I’m grateful to our associates, whose commitment to innovation and customer success continues to drive our company forward. As we close out 2026 and look ahead to 2027, we remain focused on integrating new specialty product lines, driving efficiencies, and supporting our customers and suppliers with the in-stock availability and next-day delivery capabilities they value in a more cautious demand environment.” Third Quarter 2026 Highlights 3Q 2026 3Q 2025 % change (in thousands, except per-share data and percentages) Consolidated Results Sales $ 1,802,174 $ 1,667,806 8 % Net income 36,390 21,769 67 % Net income per common share - diluted 1.04 0.58 79 % Adjusted EBITDA 1 98,489 74,381 32 % Segment Results Building Materials Distribution sales $ 1,669,465 $ 1,556,150 7 % Building Materials Distribution income 51,280 54,286 (6) % Building Materials Distribution EBITDA 1 66,902 69,831 (4) % Wood Products sales 461,236 396,401 16 % Wood Products income (loss) 16,079 (12,055) N/M Wood Products EBITDA 1 42,690 14,506 194 % 1 For reconciliations of non-GAAP measures, see summary notes at the end of this press release. In third quarter 2026, total U.S. housing starts and single-family housing starts decreased 4% and 2%, respectively, compared to the same period in 2025. On a year-to-date basis through September 2026, total U.S. housing starts and single-family housing starts decreased 1% and 4%, respectively, compared to the same period in 2025. Single-family housing starts are the key demand driver for our sales. Building Materials Distribution (BMD) BMD's sales increased $113.3 million, or 7%, to $1,669.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $1,556.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The overall increase in sales was driven by net sales price and net sales volume increases of 5% and 2%, respectively. By product line, general line product sales increased 4%, commodity sales increased 15%, and EWP sales (substantially all of which are sourced through our Wood Products segment) increased 1%. BMD segment income decreased $3.0 million to $51.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $54.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in segment income was driven by increased selling and distribution expenses of $6.9 million, offset partially by a gross margin increase of $3.6 million. The increase in gross margin was driven by higher gross margins on commodity products, offset partially by lower gross margins on general line products. Wood Products Wood Products' sales, including sales to BMD, increased $64.8 million, or 16%, to $461.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $396.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in sales was primarily driven by higher plywood sales prices and EWP sales volumes. These increases were offset partially by lower plywood sales volumes. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, Wood Products' segment income was $16.1 million compared to segment loss of $12.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in segment income was primarily due to higher plywood sales prices and EWP sales volumes, offset partially by higher per-unit conversion costs. The Company had $452.5 million of outstanding debt at September 30, 2026. 2 Capital Allocation We expect capital expenditures in 2026, excluding potential acquisition spending, to total approximately $120 million to $140 million. This level of capital expenditures could increase or decrease as a result of several factors, including availability of engineering and construction resources and timing and availability of equipment purchases. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company paid $26.1 million in common stock dividends. On October 29, 2026, our board of directors declared a quarterly dividend of $0.23 per share on our common stock, payable on December 16, 2026, to stockholders of record on December 1, 2026. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company paid $112.8 million for the repurchase of 1,466,250 shares of our outstanding common stock. In October 2026, the Company repurchased an additional 65,006 shares of our common stock at a cost of approximately $5 million. Subsequent to these share repurchases, approximately $120 million of our outstanding common stock was available for repurchase under our existing share repurchase program. Outlook Demand for the products we purchase and distribute, as well as the products we manufacture, is driven primarily by new single-family residential construction, with additional demand generated by new multi-family residential construction, residential repair-and-remodeling, and light commercial activity. During the third quarter, high fuel prices and an inflation-driven increase in benchmark interest rates amplified the affordability challenges that have constrained the new home market throughout 2026. To compensate for a reduced pool of qualified homebuyers, homebuilders have pivoted toward build-to-order construction to better align housing starts with home sales and manage finished-home inventory. Activity levels in the fourth quarter are expected to exhibit typical seasonality and decelerate through the winter. Early industry projections for 2027 indicate that housing starts are expected to decline mid-single digits from 2026 levels. Beyond the near-term uncertainty, long-term residential construction fundamentals remain positive, supported by generational tailwinds and an undersupplied housing market. High homeowner equity, aging U.S. housing stock, and a growing preference among older adults to age in place support sustained growth in repair-and-remodeling spending and reinforce the industry’s underlying demand drivers. Our distribution business, which purchases and resells a diverse range of products, may benefit from rising prices through increased sales and margins, while periods of declining prices may present challenges. Future product pricing, particularly for commodity products we distribute and manufacture, is expected to remain dynamic, influenced by economic and geopolitical conditions, duties and tariffs, input costs, industry operating rates, supply disruptions, transportation costs and availability, inventory levels, and seasonal demand patterns. Our ability to capture market share associated with recent supplier realignment is dependent upon effective execution of inventory load-in, and maintaining inventory positions sufficient to meet customer demand. Customer reliance on our distribution business increases during periods of market uncertainty, as customers respond to slowing sales with more conservative inventory practices, while greater demand certainty typically moderates this effect. We will continue to monitor end-market demand signals and align production rates and inventory stocking positions accordingly. Our integrated model and national distribution footprint position us to deliver outstanding service to our customers across a broad range of industry-leading products, including key structural products that we produce. Headquartered in Boise, Idaho, we operate more than 60 distribution and manufacturing facilities strategically located across the U.S. and Canada. Our work is powered by a dedicated team of over 7,500 people. Learn more at www.bc.com. Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures We refer to the terms EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA in this earnings release and the accompanying Quarterly Statistical Information as supplemental measures of our performance and liquidity that are not required by or presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (GAAP). We define EBITDA as income before interest (interest expense and interest income), income taxes, and depreciation and amortization. Additionally, we disclose Adjusted EBITDA, which further adjusts EBITDA to exclude the change in fair value of interest rate swaps. We also disclose Segment EBITDA, which is segment income (loss) before depreciation and amortization. We believe EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA are meaningful measures because they present a transparent view of our recurring operating performance and allow management to readily view operating trends, perform analytical comparisons, and identify strategies to improve operating performance. We also believe EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA are useful to investors because they provide a means to evaluate the operating performance of our segments and our Company on an ongoing basis using criteria that are used by our management and because they are frequently used by investors and other interested parties when comparing companies in our industry that have different financing and capital structures and/or tax rates. EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA, however, are not measures of our liquidity or financial performance under GAAP and should not be considered as alternatives to net income, income from operations, or any other performance measure derived in accordance with GAAP or as alternatives to cash flow from operating activities as a measure of our liquidity. The use of EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA instead of net income or segment income (loss) have limitations as analytical tools, including: the inability to determine profitability; the exclusion of interest expense, interest income, and associated significant cash requirements; and the exclusion of depreciation and amortization, which represent unavoidable operating costs. Management compensates for these limitations by relying on our GAAP results. Our measures of EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Segment EBITDA are not necessarily comparable to other similarly titled captions of other companies due to potential inconsistencies in the methods of calculation.
